historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (~0-1%) diverges by >30% from EPS (-39% 3yr, -10% 5yr) and FCF (-51% 3yr, +8% 5yr). Expected for a high-payout cyclical miner: earnings and FCF swing with coking-coal prices (FY2020 trough -> FY2022 peak -> FY2025 trough) while book is held flat by ~90%+ dividend payout. None of the CAGRs is a forward growth rate; the driver path is built from volumes (reserve depletion) and a mid-cycle price, not from a CAGR.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs on owner FCF (reported FCF less interest income; SBC zero): FY2020 271.4, FY2022 3,354.9, FY2025 399.1. Endpoints are cycle points, so all CAGRs are dominated by endpoint choice.

scenario_narratives.base: Mid-cycle coking-coal miner running out its reserves. FY2026 is a good year (H1 revenue +54%, ASP +16%, clean-coal volume +26%, recovery-rate gains), but the base does not capitalize it: prices normalize ~8% in FY2027 and the three Liulin mines produce ~5.4 Mt raw a year until Xingwu and Zhaiyadi exhaust in FY2033-34. With no debt and HK$9bn of net cash (~HK$1.77/share before bridge items), most of the per-share value is cash plus ~9 years of declining mine cash flows; there is essentially no terminal value.
scenario_narratives.bull: Supply-side discipline and mine-safety curtailments in Shanxi keep premium low-sulphur coking coal tight while infrastructure/'Two Priorities' spending and machinery exports hold steel demand; margins recover toward 45%. The real bull lever is reserves: the 2007 JORC estimate has never been updated, 112 Mt of in-place resource remains, and a reserve upgrade or a cash-funded acquisition of a further Shanxi mine (the rights-issue prospectus earmarked cash for 'future investment') would extend the business beyond FY2035.
scenario_narratives.bear: China's steel output keeps falling (-3.0% H1 2026), property investment keeps contracting, Mongolian imports cap prices, and the trading business dilutes margin without adding value. Prices return to FY2025 (margin ~30%), unit costs keep rising, Shougang Group (the parent and 14-34% of self-produced revenue) presses on price, and reserves run out on the 2007 schedule. Value then collapses toward cash plus a few years of thin mine cash flow.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Discount rate 12.5% (10.0% base cost of equity + 2.5pt structural premium for 3.5x peak-to-trough EBITDA cyclicality, mining-licence/reserve single point of failure and single-province concentration; see inputs.wacc_rationale), raised from 10.0% at the 2026-10-11 sanity-check fix pass. The P/E trip itself is largely a trough-earnings artefact: FY2025 EPS (HK$0.124) is the cycle low, the market price alone sits at ~22x it, and ~HK$1.53/share of the value is net cash after the bridge items that earns nothing in P/E terms; on mid-cycle FY2023-24 EPS (HK$0.30-0.38) the weighted IV is ~8-10x. A WACC premium cannot clear the P/E rule: only the mine flows are discounted, so +2.5pt moves weighted IV HK$3.03 -> HK$2.88. A depleting coking-coal asset wrapped around a large net-cash balance. Value = cash (net of declared dividends and the minorities' share) + PV of ~9-10 years of mid-cycle mine cash flows, with little or no terminal value. The valuation is NOT a growth DCF: revenue path is volume (reserve depletion) x mid-cycle price, and the terminal cap is 0-4x rather than a perpetuity.
key_risks_to_valuation: Reserve life: the 48.66 Mt recoverable reserve is a 2007 JORC estimate less output; a re-estimate could move mine life by years in either direction and is the largest single swing factor.
Coking-coal price: a 10% price move is roughly a 20-25% move in mine EBITDA at these margins.
Cash trapped in PRC subsidiaries: repatriation incurs withholding tax and the minority share is an estimate (11.35% pro-rata).
Related-party/SOE governance: Shougang Group is controlling shareholder and a major customer; capital allocation of the HK$9bn cash pile (dividends vs. acquisitions) is at the board's discretion.
Closure and restoration costs at end of mine life beyond the HK$535m restricted restoration fund.
Proposed 2026 Share Option Scheme (new-share issuance) -- provisioned at 0.2% of revenue.

inputs.wacc_rationale: All-equity (no borrowings); HKD flows (HKD peg to USD; underlying RMB coking-coal sales in Shanxi). Base cost of equity 10.0%: HK/US 10y risk-free ~3.5-4% + beta ~1.1 x ERP ~5.5-6%. PLUS a +2.5pt structural premium added at the sanity-check fix pass (2026-10-11, P/E trip), built from the additive template and applied only where the evidence qualifies: (1) extreme cyclicality +1.0 -- EBITDA FY2022 HK$5,106m vs FY2025 HK$1,451m = 3.5x peak-to-trough, above the 3x trigger; low end of the 1.0-2.0 range because commodity-price risk is also carried in the bear flows and the 25% bear weight; (2) regulatory single point of failure / reserve depletion +1.0 -- mining licences (7-17 years) are shorter than mine lives and the 48.66 Mt reserve is an unrevised 2007 JORC figure; low end because depletion itself is already modelled in the volume taper; (3) concentrated geography +0.5 -- all three mines in Liulin county, Shanxi, 100% PRC sales; low end because a single province is the norm for Chinese coal SOE-linked miners. NOT applied: customer concentration (Shougang Group 14-39% of revenue across periods, below the >40% trigger; top-5 ~53-57% is a different test) and small-cap illiquidity (market cap ~HK$14.2bn / ~US$1.8bn at 5,091m shares, well above the US$300m threshold). Total 12.5% in all three scenarios. Because ~60% of equity value is net cash (not discounted), the premium moves the per-share value much less than the rate change suggests.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: HK$37.3m lease liabilities (7.2 current + 30.1 non-current, 30 Jun 2026) in total_debt; lease principal (HK$0.8m H1 FY2026, HK$12.1m FY2025) not deducted from flows. Immaterial either way.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI charged once in the flows: cash_tax_rate_path is a combined leakage rate (PRC 25% EIT + dividend withholding + minority share of mine profits). Calibrated on FY2023/24/25: (attributable NI - after-tax interest income) / (EBITDA - D&A) = 57.7% / 57.9% / 58.3%, i.e. ~42% leakage in every year. Because consolidated cash also belongs partly to minorities, the NCI pro-rata share of cash is deducted in the equity bridge (not the NCI book equity, which would charge the mine flows twice).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF with cyclical/non-US adaptations, structured as a DEPLETING-ASSET (finite mine-life) model. Shougang Fushan is a pure coking-coal miner (three underground mines in Liulin, Shanxi: Xingwu, Jinjiazhuang, Zhaiyadi) plus a low-margin coal/materials trading business started Mar-2025 (~23% of H1 FY2026 revenue). Recoverable reserves at 31 Dec 2025 are only 48.66 Mt (Xingwu 16.04, Jinjiazhuang 17.70, Zhaiyadi 14.92; FY2025 AR line 568) against 5.25 Mt raw production in FY2025 -- ~9 years. The reserve figure is the 2007 John T. Boyd JORC estimate less cumulative output, never re-estimated. The 10-year driver path therefore tapers volume as Xingwu (~FY2033) and Zhaiyadi (~FY2034) exhaust, and terminal growth is 0 with a 0-4x terminal cap rather than a Gordon perpetuity: a perpetuity on a 9-year reserve is the single largest error available here. MID-CYCLE: FY2025 (EBITDA margin 28.7%, owner FCF HK$399m) is a trough and FY2021-23 a supercycle peak; the base runs FY2026 off H1 FY2026 actuals (revenue 3,243, EBITDA margin 41.5%, ASP RMB1,237/t incl VAT) then normalizes prices ~8% in FY2027 to a ~40% blended margin (~52% mining, ~2% trading, mix 77/23). Owner FCF = reported FCF 558.3 - SBC 0 - interest income 159.2 = 399.1 (FY2025). Interest income stripped because net cash (HK$9.0bn) is >20x the FCF base; the cash enters the bridge instead. Restricted deposits (HK$737m: HK$535m mine-restoration fund, HK$202m pledged against bills) are excluded from cash, which also covers the unprovisioned closure cost. Not modelled: PRC withholding tax if retained subsidiary cash is repatriated; mining-right renewal fees. Buybacks: none since FY2023 (HK$303m); flat count is a convention, not company-funded. Price is ex the HK$0.10 interim dividend (record date 21 Sep 2026), so the declared-unpaid dividend is deducted from the 30 Jun cash.

bear.terminal_cap_note: Intended zero residual; 0 is read by the engine as unset and defaulted to 10x, so 0.01x is used (TV ~HK$2m, immaterial).
bear.rationale: H2 FY2026 softens, then coking-coal prices revert to FY2025 levels (China crude steel output falling, property investment -18% YoY, rising Mongolian imports); unit cost inflation (+17% YoY in H1 FY2026) persists so the blended margin sits near FY2025's 29%. Reserves deplete on the JORC figure with an earlier taper (Xingwu from FY2032); zero residual.

base.rationale: FY2026 = H1 actual 3,243 + H2 ~3,200 (management expects a 'more balanced' H2 market) = ~6,450. FY2027 prices normalize ~8%; then ~+1%/yr price against flat volume ~5.4 Mt raw. Volume taper: Xingwu exhausts ~FY2033, Zhaiyadi ~FY2034, leaving Jinjiazhuang (~2 Mt remaining after FY2035) -- hence the 1x residual cap. Margin falls in the tail as fixed costs spread over less tonnage. D&A 11% (FY2023-25 10.9-11.9%; mining-right amortization runs on units of production). Capex 7.5% sustaining (FY2023-25 7.1-8.9%) tapering to ~1% as mines approach closure.

bull.rationale: Tight domestic supply persists (safety inspections, Shanxi output down, Mongolian import bottlenecks): prices hold ~FY2026 levels and margin returns toward the 2018-20 mining norm. A re-estimate of the 2007 JORC reserves (112 Mt in-place remains) extends mine life, so the taper is gentler and a 4x residual is paid for the remaining tonnage.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 1x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (above the 15% default): single-commodity price exposure, a single province/regulator, a related-party anchor customer and a hard reserve limit. Base 50%: central mid-cycle case. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): it needs two independent things -- sustained high coking-coal prices AND a reserve extension or accretive acquisition -- and the company has not re-estimated reserves since 2007.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.

diagnosis.detail: Structural risks in the qualitative analysis that a standard WACC may not price: customer concentration, cyclicality, regulatory single point of failure

sanity_check.fix_applied: WACC premium +2.5pt (10.0%->12.5% all scenarios): +1.0pt extreme cyclicality (FY2022 EBITDA HK$5,106m vs FY2025 HK$1,451m, 3.5x peak-to-trough), +1.0pt regulatory single point of failure (mining licenses 7-17yr, reserves on unrevised 2007 estimate), +0.5pt geographic concentration (all 3 mines in Liulin, Shanxi; all sales in China). Customer-concentration and small-cap-illiquidity premiums not applied (Shougang Group 14-39% of revenue, below the 40% trigger; market cap ~US$1.8bn, above the $300m small-cap trigger). Exit-multiple cap (#4) not stacked on top -- the ~9yr reserve-life taper already caps terminal value at 1x base/4x bull EV/EBITDA, both within the 10yr historical range.
sanity_check.fix_note: Trip persists after the one budgeted fix pass (P/E 22.8x vs 19.1x limit = 2x the 9.5x 10yr average). Treated as a known false positive, not a second fix: FY2025 EPS (HK$0.124) is the cycle trough and itself prints the 10yr-high P/E of 26.6x; ~HK$1.53/share of the HK$2.88 weighted IV is net cash (after dividends and minority interests) that a P/E ratio is not built to price. On mid-cycle FY2023-24 EPS (HK$0.30-0.38) the IV implies ~8-10x, inside the historical range.
